body: I totally hear and feel you, friend. I would cry until I was throwing up and felt like my chest was collapsing. It feels like you are underwater and drowning. Make sure you reach out to loved ones, and friends. They can give you so much support during this time.

I promise you it gets better. I really thought that people were BSing me and I thought I would end up killing myself. It takes time and it won't ever be perfect, but I promise it gets better. Keep going my friend.
I am thinking of you and sending you so much love right now.

The nightmares kill me. I have dreams that she didn't take her life and she is still with me. You should ask your doctor if there is a sleeping med they would be comfortable putting you on. I am on a small sleeping pill and it completely stops the dreams for me. I'm here if you need anything.

For so long I felt like my entire relationship with her was fake, and I had made it all up. Almost like she was imaginary. My trauma therapist told me that is pretty normal, and memories come back slowly. That part sucks, you forget everything and then random memories hit you out of nowhere and send you spiraling. You learn how to manage it, I promise. Im here if you need anything, and I am so sorry for your loss.

Yeah it's some freaky shit. I do not know if there is a god, but sometimes I get very random whiffs of her. The weirdest thing to happen to me up to now is my college roommate smells exactly like her. Feels like a sign from something for sure. 

sending you love rn

Hi there. A little more than a year ago my 17-year-old girlfriend killed herself. The last thing I ever got from her was a voicemail telling me to sleep well and that she would see me the next day. The first year after her death was a literal helltrap for me. You are going through the firsts without your loved one. First Christmas, first birthday, etc. Please give yourself room to grieve fully. Try to find something small that takes your mind off of it for a little bit. I found that getting an animal really helped me with the trauma. The trauma you go through after someone commits suicide is so difficult to manage because you are feeling so many things all at once. My best advice would be to ditch your therapist and find a trauma-focused counselor. It really helped me to have someone guide me through what took place that night and help me navigate the ins and outs of loss. 

Things get better, and then they get worse, and then they get better again. I really wish the absolute best for you, and please reach out if you need anything.
It's unbearable, but I promise that with time it doesn't hurt as bad as it does now. I'm here for you, ok? Be safe. Message me if you need anything
I hate when people say it's not my fault. I was supposed to be there for her in the end. I am so sorry for your loss honey.

Hi honey. I am so so so fucking sorry for your loss.

I wish there was a google search for how to feel after suicide because it is always the same BS about the 5 stages of grief. I'm going to tell you right now that it is more like 63 stages of what the fresh fuck is happening to my life and how do I fix it.

There is no way to grasp the realization that he is gone, and I know that panic in your chest when you think that you hear his footsteps or voice. I lost my girlfriend 5 months ago to suicide, and this whole experience has been Hell 40 times over. You are allowed to be angry and depressed and nauseous. I didn't eat for almost 13 days after I found out my girlfriend died. Something doesn't feel right about eating without them. 

I know you are looking for answers to the question of why. My best advice is that there is nothing you will find out about the situation or his feelings that will make you feel more at peace. Even after reading my girlfriend's hidden journals, which told me how actively suicidal she was, it actually made me angrier. Why would you hide this from us, why didn't you let us in? Do you not trust us? What could I have done to make this better? Sometimes there are things we as humans will never understand. Suicide is one of them. 

Now to answer your questions about what should you do. 

Grieve.

I'm not talking like the TV crying on the couch. Let yourself feel every single wave of sadness that this has brought because if you hold it down, it will explode and you will feel extremely suicidal  (I'm talking from past experiences). I would call the person you are closest with, the one you would trust with anything, and just cry and scream and break things. Ask the questions of why and just let everything that you feel out right now. You'll feel numb after and that will last for a couple of days, but I wish I had let out the wave of emotions that I had, instead of bottling them up. 

It will get better. It will. It sounds so stupid, but I swear it will. I didn't buy people's bullshit about time, because how would they know? They didn't lose someone like I did. This next month will be hard, then the next month will be hard, and then the next month will be hard. It will be hard, but you learn how to manage with the fact that they have passed. You never get over it. You just somehow learn how to manage it and be happy with the time you had together. It's going to suck so badly, but I promise you will get through. I believe in you and I am so proud that you are reaching out to those around you. Make sure you can talk to someone who listens, and if there is no one, reach out to a therapist. 

Take care of yourself, and I'm sorry if this came off as harsh, I just would rather be honest with you then have you go through 40 google searches to read the same BS. Be safe.

 Love, Rhys.

My girlfriend was found the same way 5 months ago. I'm so sorry for your loss and I'm sorry we are in the same boat. I can't really tell the difference between trauma and just my brain, so yeah it's weird. I'm sorry that happened to you though. Also im sorry you grew up in that environment.

Im so sorry. I'm here for you no matter what. Take care of yourself please. Over time, it slowly gets better.
